description: A group of engineers interested in solving problems related to both space and technology
summary:
Our project focuses on developing a health monitoring device that helps astronauts track their well being during space missions. Living in low gravity and being isolated for long periods can affect an astronaut's health, both physically and mentally; so we want to create a system to monitor these changes more easily.
We plan to develop a wearable cuff that uses sensor technology to collect body measurements and vitals. The main problems our project will target are tracking elevated pulse rate and radiation exposure. Other supported body measurements could help estimate sleep duration and hydration levels. This data is stored in a chip, where astronauts will input the collected information to our website, created using GoDaddy. There, astronauts can view their health information and track changes over time.
For mental health, astronauts will be able to complete daily check ins or utilize journal entries about how they're feeling, on said website. Our goal is to organize important health information in one place, and help astronauts recognize potential health concerns while adjusting to the challenges of living in space.
details:
• What exactly does it do? 

Our project is a health monitoring system designed for astronauts. It collects and combines physical health data from a wearable cuff, radiation exposure data from existing dosimeter technology, and mental health check-ins into one website. The system helps astronauts view their health trends over time and identify possible concerns during long duration space missions. 

• How does it work? 

Our system integrates a radiation dosimeter and health monitoring sensors into one wearable cuff. The dosimeter measures the astronaut's radiation exposure, while the other sensors collect physical health data, such as heart rate. All the measurements are stored on a chip within the cuff, which can then be connected to a computer, where the data is uploaded to our website that organizes trends and highlights potential concerns.

The website organizes the information into graphs and charts, allowing astronauts to track changes in their health and radiation exposure over time. It would also highlight unusual readings that may require attention. Also, astronauts can manually complete daily check ins to record their mood and stress levels, acting as a self therapy mechanism.

• What benefits does it have? 

Our system makes health monitoring easier and more convenient by combining multiple measurements into one device, and one website. It helps astronauts identify potential health concerns earlier, and supports their mental well being during isolation.

• What do you hope to achieve? 

We hope to improve astronaut safety by making health monitoring more convenient and accessible. Our goal is to help astronauts recognize health concerns early and make better informed decisions during space missions.

• What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

We plan to use GoDaddy to build our website

We also used google sheets and google forms for portions of our website.
